note:
SALVAGE RITES — the scrapyard on Ironside Street, and the street's one real vertical.

⚠ IT IS BOUND BY NAME AND REPLACES NOTHING, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON IT IS A FILE. `type:junkyard`
draws FOUR buildings — Slag & Wares, Thumb On The Scale and The Houndyard as well as this one — so
redesigning the arm would redesign three yards nobody asked about, in three other districts. A name
bind takes this tile and leaves the type alone, which is the house rule for a twin.

⚠ THE CRANE IS ADORNMENT AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. A lattice derrick is the tallest thing on Ironside
Street and it is also open steel you can see the sky through: as mass it would enter CFIT collision,
the ground probe and the occluder hulls as a solid block, and a truck would hit a yard full of air.
`latticeTower` draws it as strokes, which is both the honest shape and the free one.

⚠ AND THE BALES ARE MASS, BECAUSE THEY ARE. Crushed cars stacked two storeys high is a wall — you
cannot drive through it and it throws a real shadow — so the stacks are boxes and they are what the
yard is actually made of. The office is the smallest object on the tile, on purpose.

⚠ THE CONTAINERS ARE WHAT MAKES IT READ AS A YARD, AND THE REASON IS COLOUR RATHER THAN SHAPE. This
was five brown boxes — `ty_junk_bale` is [126,72,44] and `ty_slag` [74,60,50] — beside a `ty_junk_shack`
office at [104,84,62], on redrock, at the end of a street of brick. Every mass on the tile was the same
hue within a few points, so the whole thing read as one brown lump with a mast on it, and no amount of
geometry fixes that. Two stacked boxes take the container palettes (`ty_cont_r`, `ty_cont_y`, `ty_cont_b`)
and the yard now has the three saturated accents nothing else on Ironside Street has. The CRUSHED CARS
stay brown, which is what they are — the point is that they are now brown NEXT TO something.

⚠ A CONTAINER IS LONG AND A BOX IS SQUARE UNLESS YOU SAY OTHERWISE. `box` takes `fd` — the half-depth —
and it defaults to `hw`, so a container asked for at `hw: 0.30` is a 0.6-square cube and reads as a
warehouse. Every stacked box here carries an explicit `fd`.

⚠ THE TORCH IS A GLINT BY DAY AND A LIGHT AT NIGHT, WHICH IS WHAT `s` CONTROLS. `AUTHORED_ADORN.glowPool`
takes no night term — unlike `neonBlade`, `marqueeBand` and the rest — so a glow sized to read as a
cutting torch after dark is a white blob in full sun. `s: 7` is under the size of the thing it sits on,
which is the rule: a glint by day, a bloom at night.

⚠ AND THE YARD SAYS ITS NAME ONCE. The board over the door carries the name, a crane hook (`picto: 'hook'`)
and nothing else; 廢料 — scrap material — goes on a blade round the corner, which is a SECOND SIGN and not
a second name. `junkyard` is in UNSIGNED_TRADE, so the derived kit will not letter this building at all
and both of these are authored: the kit is right that a yard's name is on the gate, and this one's gate
is its office door.
